messages:
maria: Quick repro for a weird reqid/redaction flip in the Rust sampleapp when auth retry increases log level to debug. Seeing req_id in trace but <redacted> in some log lines.

sam: Can you drop the repro steps and a tiny log snippet? @alex might have seen something similar.

maria: Steps:
1) checkout `sample-rust` branch `feat/telemetry-redact`
2) env: `REDACT=1 OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4317 LOG_LEVEL=info`
3) `cargo run --bin sampleapp`
4) hit `/login` repeatedly until upstream returns a 401 then a 200 (we use a flaky test auth to force a retry)

Observed logs (condensed):
```
INFO  auth::handler: login attempt; user=alice req_id=abcd1234
DEBUG http::retry: retrying auth; attempt=2
INFO  auth::handler: retry succeeded; user=alice req_id=<redacted>
```
But the span for the request (otel) contains `req_id=abcd1234` and the trace shows it consistently. Only some log events become redacted.

maria: Quick local diff that reproduces (logger init order):
```rust
// problematic ordering
tracing_subscriber::registry()
  .with(tracing_log::LogTracer::new())
  .with(EnvFilter::new("info"))
  .with(otel_layer)
  .with(RedactionLayer::new())
  .init();
```
If I move `RedactionLayer` before `otel_layer` or attach the req_id to the span explicitly, the redaction becomes consistent.

alex: This smells like layer ordering + async batching in the otel exporter. The redaction layer is running at formatting time and expects req_id to be present on the event context. When the retry path temporarily switches log level / path it emits before span fields are attached to the event, so the redactor falls back to redacting by default.

alex: Two quick fixes:
- Attach `req_id` as a span field as early as possible: `span!(Level::INFO, "request", req_id = %req_id)` so later layers can read it reliably.
- Reorder layers so the tracing/span-to-otel conversion happens after we capture fields, or make redaction consult span fields rather than raw event text.

katie: Can we make the sampleapp default to the safe ordering and add a comment explaining why? This will bite folks on onboarding.

maria: Confirmed local workaround: add `scope.with_span()` and set the req_id into the span before calling the HTTP client -> logs stable.

sam: I'll open a PR against `sample-rust` to reorder the subscriber layers, add a test that flips loglevel during a retry, and add a short note in the quickstart.

infra-bot: Created INFRA-2143: "rust sampleapp: make req_id propagation + redaction deterministic during retries" (link: https://redwood.internal/INFRA-2143)

katie: Amazing, thanks @sam :tada:

maria: Leaving the repro steps + log snippets in the ticket. If anyone hits it on other runtimes (node/go) please paste logs there so we can generalize the fix.

sam: Will do a cross-runtime sweep after the PR.
